newsitem.title: USA: PSC to restructure scanner manufacturing.
newsitem.headline: PSC to restructure scanner manufacturing.

text.p: PSC Inc said Monday that it plans to consolidate all its manufacturing of new handheld scanners and scan modules at its Eugene, Oregon facility and move the manufacturing of its U-Scan Express self-checkout systems to its Webster, New York plant.

The company also said that the Eugene plant, which also manufactures retail fixed position products, will focus on high volume production, while the Webster plant will focus on lower volume, customized industrial fixed position products and verification products, as well as the U-Scan Express systems.
The company added that it would pay its recently-named chief executive, Robert Strandberg, substantially all of his compensation in stock options, to align his interests with the shareholders.
PSC shares closed Monday at 7-3/8, up 3/8 over Friday's close.

Monday, the company reported second-quarter loss of $2.7 million, or $0.24 per share. The loss included a pre-tax charge of $4.2 million, which included severance payments to several former senior executives and restructuring charges. The company also took a $1 million charge for discontinuing some product lines.
PSC said these changes will save it about $6 million on an annualized basis.
The company makes laser based handheld and fixed position bar code scanners, bar code engines and verifiers and automated carton dimensioning systems.
